title: A Bridge for the Orchard
premise: In the river city of Vellamark, on the eve of a printers' revolution, Juniper Ashgrove has survived twelve years in her father's print shop by mastering silence. When a frightened child named Wren is left at their door carrying a hidden plate of type that implicates a magistrate in the disappearance of striking workers, Juniper must choose between invisibility and justice. With her father arrested and checkpoints sealing the city, she gathers an unlikely found family—a defected soldier, a blind archivist, and the child herself—to smuggle the evidence to the underground press before the magistrate burns it. The book ends with the truth printed and scattered across the city at dawn, Juniper's father freed, and Juniper finally speaking her own name aloud without fear.
about_author: Zephyrine Thackeray is the pen name of a former letterpress restorer who spent a decade cataloguing banned pamphlets in municipal archives. She writes historical fiction about the people history forgot to record.

chapters.title: The Weight of Quiet
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Establishes the print shop, her father Aldous's typeface work, and the rules of silence she learned after her mother vanished. She notices soldiers measuring doorways for new checkpoints. Emotional beat: the comfort of routine already fraying.

chapters.title: A Child at the Door
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A girl, Wren, is left at the shop with a wrapped bundle and a note: forget the face. Inside is a leaden printing plate bearing names Juniper recognizes—workers declared 'relocated.' Emotional beat: dread blooming into reluctant responsibility.

chapters.title: What the Plate Says
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Aldous. Father and daughter decode the plate: it was cast from the magistrate Corvane's private press, proof he ordered disappearances. Aldous insists they must destroy it; Juniper secretly disagrees. Beat: first fracture between safety and conscience.

chapters.title: The Knock at Midnight
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Soldiers arrest Aldous for sedition they cannot yet prove, taking him to the Graykeep. They miss the plate, hidden in a forme of wedding invitations. Beat: terror sharpening into resolve; Juniper stops being invisible by choice.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She maps the city's sealed bridges and gates, learning the route evidence must travel to reach the underground press in the orchard district. Beat: cold planning as armor against grief.

chapters.title: The Blind Archivist
chapters.summary: Maren's POV introduced. Maren, who memorizes banned texts by touch, recognizes the plate's typeface as her brother's—the first disappeared worker. She joins Juniper. Beat: two keepers of memory finding each other.

chapters.title: A Soldier Who Looked Away
chapters.summary: Davor's POV introduced. A checkpoint guard haunted by the night of the relocations seeks out the print shop, offering passage through his gate—for a price he won't name yet. Beat: guilt reaching toward redemption.

chapters.title: Wren Speaks
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The child finally reveals how she got the plate: her mother pressed it into her hands and told her to run. Beat: grief made small and enormous; Juniper promises the names will be read aloud.

chapters.title: The Wedding Invitations
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A raid nearly finds the plate; Juniper prints decoy invitations over it and talks her way past an inspector using everything her father taught her about type. Beat: competence as courage; first real victory.

chapters.title: Corvane's Offer
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. The magistrate, aware a plate exists, offers Aldous freedom for its return—and sends a threatening note to Juniper. Beat: the antagonist revealed as bureaucratic evil, patient and certain.

chapters.title: The Price Davor Names
chapters.summary: Davor's POV. His price: that his name appear in whatever is printed, so his complicity is not erased. Juniper agrees. Beat: justice outside the law includes accountability; trust cemented.

chapters.title: Learning the Orchard Road
chapters.summary: Juniper and Maren's POV, alternating. They rehearse the smuggling route through the flooded tanneries and the old orchard, where Wren's mother once worked. Beat: found family forming around shared purpose.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Type Case
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. An apprentice Juniper trusted sells information to Corvane; the shop is watched. They must move the plate tonight or lose everything. Beat: betrayal cutting deep, but clarifying who truly stands with them.

chapters.title: Through the Tanneries
chapters.summary: Davor's POV. The first checkpoint crossing goes wrong; Davor shoots no one but takes a beating to cover their escape. Beat: sacrifice without glory; the cost becomes real.

chapters.title: What Memory Keeps
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Hiding in the archivist's cellar, Maren recites the disappeared workers' names to Wren so the child can carry them too. Beat: memory as inheritance; tenderness at the story's center.

chapters.title: The Second Gate
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. At the bridge checkpoint, Juniper hides the plate inside a coffin being ferried to the orchard cemetery, walking beside mourners who know and say nothing. Beat: solidarity of strangers; quiet heroism of ordinary people.

chapters.title: Corvane Closes the Net
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. He orders the orchard burned at dawn and moves Aldous's execution up. A captured apprentice reveals the press's location. Beat: the walls closing in; despair before the climb.

chapters.title: Night in the Orchard
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The group reaches the underground press as soldiers surround the orchard. They set type by lamplight—Wren placing each name herself. Beat: the calm before the storm; purpose transfiguring fear.

chapters.title: Ink Before Dawn
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. As fires approach, they print hundreds of broadsheets naming Corvane's victims and crimes. Davor holds the gate; Maren guides them out by memory when lanterns fail. Beat: climax—everything risked for the truth made physical.

chapters.title: Paper on the Wind
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At dawn, citizens scatter the broadsheets across the city; crowds gather at the Graykeep reading names aloud. Corvane's authority dissolves as soldiers refuse orders. Beat: catharsis; the silence broken everywhere at once.

chapters.title: The Door of the Graykeep
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper walks into the collapsing regime's headquarters and demands her father—not begging, but citing the now-public evidence. Aldous walks free; Corvane is taken by his own guards. Beat: justice achieved outside the law, then ratified by it.

chapters.title: A Bridge for the Orchard
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, epilogue weeks later. The shop reopens; the orchard district rebuilds its burned rows; a footbridge is raised in the disappeared workers' names. Juniper sets a new typeface—her own design—and prints Wren's mother's name first. Beat: resolution; memory kept, family chosen, voice found.
